scopeDecisions.recommendation: Use behavioral conditions rather than a raw API-method denominator; each declared transaction surface must map to exactly one condition.
Keep query execution inside a transaction here, following the FS-QUERY-INDEX Q4d decision; ordinary query semantics stay with FS-QUERY-INDEX.
Count the atomic visibility of all writes in one transaction commit on native Listen here; SDK callback delivery belongs to FS-LISTEN-SDK.
scopeDecisions.decision: The atomic visibility of a transaction commit on native Listen is assigned to FS-TRANSACTION; SDK callback shape is assigned to FS-LISTEN-SDK.

scopeDecisions.recommendation: Count the named idle and total transaction time limits in their expiry conditions; transaction size belongs to FS-DATA-WRITE.
scopeDecisions.decision: Idle and total time limits are assigned to their transaction expiry conditions; transaction size is assigned to FS-DATA-WRITE.

scopeDecisions.recommendation: Use the sandbox conformance-harness process with clean-context corpus/runner review, two recordings and one JSONL ledger line per run. The old single-run O8 manifest is preparation material only; do not import O7/O8 Gate or reservation tooling. A fresh owner go-ahead remains necessary under the current production-send hold.
Retain historical fireemu-35fe6 recordings as immutable reference only; require sandbox evidence or an explicit owner decision before calling any historical-only condition VERIFIED.
Keep SDK-driven retry distinct from backend retry-token semantics. Do not exclude it on the strength of REST or gRPC observations.
scopeDecisions.decision: Keep SDK retry separate from backend retry-token behavior.

remainingBoundaries: The exact idle threshold is not identified: it lies between the last accepted measured idle (lower bound 110.70 s) and the first refused one (upper bound 122.96 s). Strict's 120 s limit lies inside that interval; it accepts the unobserved 113.12 to 120 s gap and refuses the unobserved 120 to 120.54 s gap.

The native gRPC sweeps (P10-A, P10-B, P10-C) are published and bound to this condition in recordedComparison, and the REST idle rows (E04) were replayed at 121 s of idle on the strict release binary (releaseReplay; the recorded idle for the commit and the rollback, a lower idle with the same outcome for the lock release).

recordedComparison.boundaryRuling: Idle and lifetime boundaries: the idle threshold is judged by the interval production narrowed, [110.70, 122.96) s (ledger 809 (5)), and strict's 120 s idle limit lies inside it; the age at which an expired token is forgotten is judged by (298.7, 302.2] s, which holds strict's 300 s of memory. Strict's 270 s total lifetime is supported by the rows themselves, not by an interval: live reads at token ages up to 253.3 s answered 0 and the first refusals came at 280.4 s, so production's lifetime lies in about (253.3, 280.4] s and 270 s lies inside it.

conditions.historicalNote: REST subset (E04): the three idle observations (commit, rollback and lock release after an idle expiry) were replayed on the strict release binary at 121 s of idle on the control clock. For the commit and the rollback that lies inside the idle production measured in both recordings (120.35 to 121.15 s and 120.60 to 121.06 s); the lock release idled 124.7 to 125.2 s in production, and strict refuses every idle above its 120 s limit, so the replay at 121 s decides the same refusal (a valid sample, not the recorded idle). Every case and post state matches both recordings (record fs-transaction-expiry-retry-04-release-replay-v1). Native gRPC sweeps (P10-B, nominal idle 65 to 70 s; P10-C, 75 to 120 s; each recorded twice) accepted every Commit through a nominal 110 s idle and refused the 120 s Commit with code 10, expired or no longer valid. The measured idle of the accepted 110 s Commit was [110.58, 113.12] s and of the refused 120 s Commit [120.54, 122.97] s. The REST refusal in the recorded run had idled about 121 s (idleSeconds 121.15 and 120.35), not the nominal 70 s wait. The exact idle threshold is not identified: it lies in [110.70, 122.96) s. Strict takes 120 s as a provisional limit, strict accepts the unobserved 113.12 to 120 s gap and refuses the unobserved 120 to 120.54 s gap. Private sandbox observation, cited by run-directory name only: P13a fs-transaction-p13a-inferred-answers-da25f2aa72b95011 (REST, two agreeing recordings): a token that idled out for 130 s answered reads at a token age of 132.4 to 135.1 s and 234.2 to 237.0 s with 10 and the expired text, a Rollback at 286.1 to 289.2 s with 10 and a read after it with 10, and a second such token answered a read at 309.3 to 312.2 s with 3 "Invalid transaction.": an idle-expired token is remembered until about 300 s of its token age like a lifetime-expired one, then forgotten (recorded over REST only: over gRPC the same memory is inferred, because the store applies one rule to both transports).
